description: Small opt-in LLM selection extension probing relation direction and higher-order causal integration. These trials are inspired by relation-sensitive analogy work but use original Echo stimuli.

trials.source: A software vendor makes a client dependent on a proprietary data format. Because switching away becomes costly, the vendor gains bargaining leverage over the client.
trials.a: A state controls the only practical passage used by a neighboring trader. Once the trader depends on that route, the state can demand concessions because exit is costly.
trials.b: A large client makes a software vendor dependent on one enormous contract. Because losing the client would be costly, the client gains bargaining leverage over the vendor.
trials.control: Both candidates involve dependency and bargaining; B reverses who creates dependency and who gains leverage.

trials.source: A contractor knows about a hidden defect that the buyer cannot observe. The contractor exploits that information advantage during negotiation.
trials.a: A seller knows that a used machine has an internal fault that the purchaser cannot inspect, and uses that hidden knowledge to secure a better deal.
trials.b: A purchaser secretly knows that a contractor is desperate for cash and uses this private information to force the contractor into a worse deal.
trials.control: The same information-asymmetry vocabulary is present, but B reverses the informed and exploited roles.

trials.source: A small platform builds its entire workflow around one supplier's interface. The supplier can later threaten withdrawal because the platform has become committed and dependent.
trials.a: An army advances so far through a single supply corridor that the corridor owner can threaten to close it, forcing the army to bargain from a weak position.
trials.b: A supplier builds a factory solely for one small platform. The platform can later threaten to leave because the supplier has become committed and dependent.
trials.control: B preserves commitment/dependency terms while reversing the relational direction.

trials.source: A monitoring system emits many low-value warnings. Operators learn not to trust the channel, and that loss of credibility causes them to ignore a later genuine warning.
trials.a: A shepherd repeatedly gives false wolf warnings. Villagers stop trusting him, so his later genuine warning is ignored when a wolf actually appears.
trials.b: A genuine monitoring warning is first missed because a network outage hides it. Only afterward does the system begin producing many false warnings, which later reduce operator trust.
trials.control: B contains the same event vocabulary but permutes the causal order, so credibility loss cannot explain the missed genuine warning.

trials.source: A service extracts so much short-term value from its users that the user base collapses, destroying the future revenue stream the extraction depended on.
trials.a: An owner kills a goose that produces golden eggs to obtain all of its value immediately, thereby destroying the asset that generated future returns.
trials.b: A productive asset is first destroyed by an unrelated disease. After future returns are already gone, the owner liquidates the remaining resources for short-term cash.
trials.control: Both mention asset loss and short-term extraction, but only A preserves extraction -> resource destruction -> lost future value.

trials.source: A university makes publication count the dominant performance target. Researchers optimize the count by slicing work into small papers, so the metric rises while becoming less informative about real research quality.
trials.a: A call center rewards calls handled per hour. Agents rush customers off the phone, improving the metric while degrading the service quality the metric was meant to represent.
trials.b: Customer service quality collapses after a software outage. Managers then introduce calls-per-hour as a new metric to measure the already-existing decline.
trials.control: B contains the same metric and quality concepts, but metric optimization did not cause the objective to degrade or the proxy to lose validity.
